title: feat(service-analytics)!: refuse a deriving aggregate over a field type that cannot carry it, for every field type and not only the temporal class
body:
Fixes #16099

## ⭐ Read this first: the cut is by AGGREGATE KIND, not by field class

`sum` / `avg` **derive** a new number from the stored values. `min` / `max` **select** one of
them and return the source field's own type. This gate judges the first pair over **every**
field type and does **not** judge the second pair at all.

⛔ **Do not "complete" this later by adding the string classes to the same gate.** Doing so
reds 15 shipped end-to-end cases, and the reason is measured below: it is not only the string
rows — `min` x `json` and `min` x `formula` are refused by the table, sit in no ruling's
scope, and are driven by the same shared fixture, so the `min` / `max` rows are ONE question
and they belong to #17513.

## ⭐ The driven measurement came first, and it is not a zero

The dispatch's first falsifier was that this card's residual might not exist: the seat's
reading of `assertAggregateFieldTypeCompatible`'s early return was **from source, not
driven**, and 「a zero here would be the interesting answer」. So it was driven before a
line was written, through the real `AnalyticsService.queryDataset` door with the
`sourceFieldMeta` hook a host wires:

```
DRIVE-NAMED    sum x text      table refuses the pair = true   threw = NO   sql_emitted = 1
DRIVE-SWEEP    6 aggregates x 49 field types = 294 pairs
               refused by the table            155
               minus temporal (#16778's)         6
               minus (min|max) x string classes 42
               RESIDUAL                        107   accepted by the compile leg today: 107 of 107
DRIVE-CONTROL  avg x datetime / date / time    DATASET_INVALID / 400, sql_emitted = 0
```

⇒ **The residual is real and total.** The named instance `sum` x a `text` field compiles and
**emits SQL**, reaching the driver. The firing control is what makes the 107 a reading of
the tree rather than of a blind harness: the same service, the same door and the same hook
see the three pairs #16778 already enforces refused, with no statement emitted.

⚠️ One correction worth recording, because the first drive lied: the initial probe reported
all 107 pairs **refused**, which would have been the interesting zero. The refusals were a
ZodError from the probe's own fixture (a one-character measure `name`, below the schema's
2-character minimum), not the gate. A reading taken one step earlier would have closed this
card as already done.

## The residual set, enumerated, with the subtraction shown

| | pairs | who owns it |
|---|---:|---|
| refused by `AGGREGATE_FIELD_TYPE_COMPATIBILITY` | 155 | the table (`@objectstack/spec`, #16353) |
| − the temporal rows | 6 | **already enforced** by #16737 / PR #16778 |
| − `min` / `max` x the string classes | 42 | **#17513** — ruled to be AMENDED, not executed |
| = residual | **107** | |
| … of which `sum` / `avg` x every field type the table refuses | **75** | **this PR** |
| … of which `min` / `max` x the non-string classes | **32** | **reported, not enforced** — see below |

The 6 / 42 / 75 / 32 split is asserted in the suite, not narrated, so a row moving upstream
moves the numbers rather than leaving a stale claim here.

## ⚠️ The subtraction the dispatch named was NOT sufficient — measured, not reasoned

The dispatch fenced one subtraction as load-bearing: enforcing `min` / `max` over
`text` / `select` / `lookup` / `autonumber` would red the 15 end-to-end cases
`__tests__/measure-result-type.test.ts` pins through `queryDataset`. That is true. It is
also not the whole fence, and the difference was found by building the full-residual
variant and running it:

```
variant: judge every non-temporal pair EXCEPT (min|max) x the string classes
result : Test Files 1 failed (1) | Tests 15 failed | 106 passed (121)
cause  : every one of the 15 failed on the same pair --
         applies aggregate "min" to field "payload", which object "duly_task" declares as `json`
```

`min` x `json` (and `min` x `formula` behind it) are refused by the table, are in **no
ruling's scope** — #17513's own text excludes non-string pairs, and this card's re-scope
excluded only 「the non-temporal pairs the table refuses that nothing depends on」 — and are
nonetheless driven end to end by the **same shared fixture** as the string rows. That
fixture compiles every measure in ONE dataset, so a single refused pair reds the whole
section.

⇒ The `min` / `max` population is **one question**, and it is not this card's to partly
execute. Reported below; ⛔ not broken here.

## What this PR changes

The gate's scope is re-cut from a FIELD class to an AGGREGATE class, and the new scope is a
strict superset of the old one:

- **Before:** judge a pair only when the field is `date` / `datetime` / `time`. Since the
  table accepts `min` / `max` over the temporal class, the set this actually refused was
  `sum` / `avg` x the 3 temporal types = **6 pairs**.
- **After:** judge a pair when its aggregate DERIVES a number (`sum` / `avg`), for **every**
  declared field type = **81 pairs** (the same 6, plus the 75 residual ones).
- `min` / `max` SELECT one of the stored values and are not judged here at all.

That line is the one this package already draws: `measureResultType` branches on exactly
`min` / `max`, because those return a value of the source field's own type while
`sum` / `avg` always return a number (#15768). The defect is about a DERIVED number whose
value is decided by the dialect rather than by the data, so the deriving aggregates are
precisely its population — a class, not a hand list of field types.

⛔ **No table row is restated anywhere.** The verdict is still
`isAggregateCompatibleWithFieldType`'s; the new `DERIVING_AGGREGATES` constant is a SCOPE
and says so in its own TSDoc. `packages/spec` is untouched by this diff.

Also in scope, because the widened reach made the old text wrong:

- `sum` x `percent` is refused at last — the row `analytics-service.ts` has called
  "incoherent" in a comment since before the table existed. `avg` x `percent` stays
  ACCEPTED by the same table, which is what makes it a row and not a class; both halves are
  pinned.
- The refusal's closing prescription is now chosen by the source field's class. #16778's
  temporal sentence is kept verbatim for temporal fields; a non-numeric field is pointed at
  `count` / `count_distinct`, which accept every type because they read no arithmetic off a
  value. Previously every refusal, whatever the field, ended with advice about instants and
  durations.
- `aggregate-datetime-measure-refusal.test.ts`'s header said the compile leg is scoped to
  the temporal class. True when written, false after this diff, so it is corrected rather
  than left to mislead.

## Does anything shipped use a newly-refused pair? No — with the control

Every dataset measure declared outside a test in this repository, with each field's declared
type resolved from its object definition:

| dataset | measure | field type | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `examples/app-showcase/src/ui/datasets/revenue-pulse.dataset.ts` | `sum` subtotal | `summary` | accepted |
| same | `sum` annual revenue | `currency` | accepted |
| `examples/app-showcase/src/ui/datasets/chart-gallery.dataset.ts` | `sum` / `avg` estimate | `number` | accepted |
| same | `avg` progress | `progress` | accepted |
| same | `sum` budget, `sum` spent | `currency` | accepted |
| `examples/app-crm/src/datasets/opportunity.dataset.ts` | `sum` / `avg` amount | `currency` | accepted |
| `examples/app-todo/src/datasets/task.dataset.ts` | `sum` estimated / actual hours | `number` | accepted |
| `packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-create-seeds.ts` | `count`, no field | — | accepted |

**Firing control on that zero**, same method over the same repository: applied to the TEST
corpus the scan does find residual pairs — `aggregate-datetime-measure-refusal.test.ts`'s
`sum` x a `text` field, and `measure-result-type.test.ts`'s `min` x `json` and `min` x
`formula`. So the zero above is a reading of the shipped declarations, not a blind scan.
The `min` pairs are the collision reported above; the `sum` x `text` pin is addressed next.

## RED before GREEN, proven by state

The one shipped test this diff turns red is the pin #16778 wrote **predicting exactly this
card**: 「If the gate ever widened past the temporal class, this case goes red.」 It did.

```
before the pin was re-aimed:
  pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-analytics test
  Test Files  1 failed | 107 passed (108)
  Tests       1 failed | 2312 passed (2313)
  FAIL  aggregate-datetime-measure-refusal.test.ts > ... > a `sum` over a TEXT field also compiles here
```

⛔ Not skipped, not quarantined, not relaxed. The case pinned the branch this card removes,
so it is **replaced**: same pair, same door, asserting the answer the platform now gives
(envelope `code` + `status`, the pair named in the message, and `sqls` empty so it cannot
pass on a query that merely returned nothing). Its `min` x `text` sibling is untouched and
keeps its row's ruling intact.

### Ablation — direction predicted before running, and the direction OBSERVED

Predicted: narrowing `DERIVING_AGGREGATES` to `['sum']` turns every `avg` refusal case red
in the ordinary direction (the compile succeeds and SQL IS emitted, so no case can pass
vacuously), and leaves every `sum` case, every accepted control and
`measure-result-type.test.ts` green.

Observed — this is what ran, not what was expected:

```
mutation on disk   HEAD blob 6e373d4196c69167184f1dbb5046e3bd42b675b5
                   after     dc6bed84ea0837b32cdbf026657be4df116a5fbf
                   removed-text occurrences 0   injected-text occurrences 1
ablation run       Test Files 2 failed | 1 passed (3)   Tests 19 failed | 171 passed (190)
                   13 red in aggregate-nontemporal-measure-refusal.test.ts
                      (12 avg refusals + the temporal-remedy continuity control)
                    6 red in aggregate-datetime-measure-refusal.test.ts
                      (the avg x temporal refusals, both derived cases, the class sweep)
                    0 red in measure-result-type.test.ts
restore by state   disk hash back to 6e373d41   git diff HEAD empty   git status --porcelain empty
```

Restored with `git checkout HEAD --` (⛔ never a bare `git checkout --`, which restores from
the index), under a `trap ... EXIT INT TERM` using an absolute `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`
path, and verified by STATE rather than by an exit code.

⚠️ **The `dist/` trap was checked, not assumed.** `ablation-dist-preflight --absent` confirmed
the mutation never reached the built output; and mutating `src` with no rebuild flipped 19
tests, which is itself the proof that this subject resolves from source (a same-package
relative import), not through `exports` into `dist/`.

## Changeset — decided by measurement

`@objectstack/service-analytics` declares `files: ["dist", ...]` and builds from
`src/index.ts`, which re-exports `compileDataset` from the changed module. After
`pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-analytics build`, grep of the real built output:

```
dist/index.js   "derives a NUMBER" / DERIVING_AGGREGATES    3 hits   -> the change SHIPS
dist/index.js   compileDataset   (positive control)         3 hits
dist/index.js   REFUSED_FOR_BOTH (test-only, neg. control)  0 hits
```

⇒ A changeset is owed, not `skip-changeset`. Shipped as **`minor`** with a `BREAKING`
declaration, following #16778's precedent for an accept-set narrowing under the launch-window
convention. Its ADR-0087 disposition is `already-registered`, naming the migration id #16778
registered under protocol major 18 — the prescription an affected author needs is unchanged;
only which pairs reach it widens. `check:adr-0087-registration` accepts it (exit 0).

## Clause-② — both limbs measured

Clause-②: no

- **Path limb:** the contract surface is `packages/spec/src/**` (including the error-code
  ledger and `*.zod.ts` contract schemas). This diff touches
  `packages/services/service-analytics/**` and `.changeset/` only. No hit.
- **Declaration limb:** the criterion is whether the card WIDENS the accept set or EXPANDS
  the public surface. This NARROWS it — 75 more pairs refused — and adds no export:
  `git diff` over the changed module shows no added or removed `export` line, `index.ts` is
  untouched, and both new symbols (`DERIVING_AGGREGATES`, `REMEDY_BY_SOURCE_CLASS`) are
  module-private `const`s. No hit.

This confirms the seat's claim-time declaration rather than inheriting it.

## ⛔ Two of the card's three residuals are deliberately NOT in this PR

This is a partial delivery by ruling, and a reader should not take it for a complete one:

- **Residual 1 — `min` / `max` over the string classes.** Left this card entirely; it is
  **#17513** (`domain:spec`), because the repair is an amendment to
  `AGGREGATE_FIELD_TYPE_COMPATIBILITY` itself. ⛔ Not enforced here.
- **Residual 3 — the three tiering escapes** (no `declaredFieldType` hook, a field the hook
  cannot resolve, a dotted relationship path). **Not work at all** — they are the contract,
  and they are pinned unchanged in the new suite.
- **New, found by driving this card — the `min` / `max` non-string rows (32 pairs).**
  Refused by the table, enforced nowhere, in no ruling's scope, and two of them
  (`min` x `json`, `min` x `formula`) carry a live dependency in the shared fixture. Filed
  rather than fixed; see the report on the card.

## Docs drift — answered on the bot's own tree, including the emitter-blind half

`docs-drift-check` derived 3 anchors and listed nothing, and says so itself: 「not a clean
bill of health」. On a diff that refuses input which compiled yesterday, the risk is not a
page that goes stale but **a page whose worked example is now a refusal** — which shares no
identifier with this diff and can never appear in that list. So it was hand-read.

Tree: the bot read `content/docs` from `7adb8670d` (head `c5ce46ef3` merged into base
`ad715aca5`). That tree's `content/docs` is **byte-identical** to the one read here
(`git diff --stat 7adb8670d HEAD -- content/docs` is empty), so these are answers on the
bot's tree, not on a different one.

**By example shape.** Every `sum` / `avg` occurrence in hand-written `content/docs`
(32 hits) resolved against what this gate actually judges. The gate has exactly **one** call
site — `dataset-compiler.ts` inside `compileDataset`, whose only production caller is
`AnalyticsService.registerDataset` — so only a `DatasetMeasure` is in its reach:

| shape | door | in this gate's reach? | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ui/dashboards.mdx:180`, `data-modeling/analytics.mdx:62-63` | `defineDataset` measures | **YES** | `sum` x `amount`, a money column — **accepted, not falsified** |
| `api/data-api.mdx:385-429` | `/analytics/query` with `cube:`, inferred measure `revenue_sum` | no — the Cube door, never `compileDataset` | not falsified; `revenue` is a money column either way |
| `protocol/objectql/query-syntax.mdx` (10), `data-modeling/queries.mdx` (9), `kernel/contracts/data-engine.mdx:446-447`, `api/error-catalog.mdx:213` | ObjectQL `aggregations[]` | no — `engine.aggregate` | not falsified; every field numeric |
| `data-modeling/fields.mdx:242`, `field-types.mdx:461`, `getting-started/common-patterns.mdx:114`, `field-type-decision-tree.mdx:198` | `Field.summary` roll-up | no — the roll-up door, its own predicate | not falsified; every field numeric |
| `ui/pages.mdx:28`, `ui/react-pages.mdx:456`, `deployment/validating-metadata.mdx:222` | page-block `aggregate` prop | no | not falsified |

⚠️ `api/data-api.mdx` was flagged as the one most likely to flip. It does not, and the reason
is proven rather than asserted: the guard's single call site is inside `compileDataset`, and
that page's example is the Cube door.

**By concept vocabulary** — six reads over hand-written `content/docs`, all zero:

| read | hits |
|---|---:|
| an aggregate "works on any field / any type" | 0 |
| prose stating which aggregates apply to which field types | 0 |
| prose about `fields[].type` for a measure | 0 |
| dataset-measure compilation refusing (or not refusing) anything | 0 |
| advice conflicting with the remedy sentences this refusal now emits | 0 |
| `sum` / `avg` over a temporal or text field as a RECOMMENDED shape | 0 |

**Firing controls, identical command shape, same corpus:** `aggregat` → 69 files,
`measure` → 41, `dataset` → 45, `summaryOperations` → 8. And a bracket on the refusal read:
lifting only the auto-generated `references/` exclusion moves it 0 → 2 files, so the pattern
can match in this corpus. The two hits are in `content/docs/references/`, which is
regenerated by `build-docs.ts` from `packages/spec` — untouched by this diff.

**The 9 coarse-fallback pages, each answered:** `api/data-api.mdx` (above);
`api/index.mdx` and `permissions/sharing-rules.mdx` (no aggregate or measure mention at all);
`kernel/services-checklist.mdx` and `plugins/packages.mdx` (capability bullets, no
accepted-pair claim); `protocol/objectql/query-syntax.mdx` (the ObjectQL door only — no
`defineDataset`, no `measures: [`, no `aggregate: '`); and the three release pages
`releases/implementation-status.mdx`, `releases/v17/17-0.mdx`, `releases/v9.mdx` — zero hits
on temporal / datetime-measure / cannot-carry / `DATASET_INVALID` / the card numbers, bracketed
by 4, 8 and 17 hits respectively on `analytics|measure`, so the grep shape does read them.
Those three are release-owned and would be a docs-only PR in any case.

**What the hand read DID find — a third stale narrative, fixed here.**
`__tests__/formula-return-type-measure.test.ts` explained why `min` / `max` over a `formula`
field is still reachable by quoting the temporal early return this diff removes. The
conclusion survives (`min` / `max` are outside the gate either way); the reason moved from
the field class to the aggregate class, and the header now says so.

**Already-declared, not a new finding:** `/analytics/query` reached with a raw `cube:` does
not pass through `compileDataset`, so an incompatible pair arriving as an inferred measure
(`revenue_sum`) is not judged. #16778 already named that uncovered face when it landed this
gate; this diff neither widens nor narrows it.

## Tests

Measured at `7662a755a`, the final commit. Heavy runs through `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`,
quoted by its own verdict line.

| run | verdict |
|---|---|
| dependency closure build (`--filter '@objectstack/service-analytics^...'`) | `VERDICT command-exit 0` |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-analytics test` | `VERDICT command-exit 0` — **109 files, 2358 tests, 0 failed** |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-analytics typecheck` | `VERDICT command-exit 0` |
| `pnpm build` (whole repo, to satisfy three gate prerequisites) | `VERDICT command-exit 0` — 73 of 73 tasks |

`tsc --noEmit --listFiles` names `aggregate-nontemporal-measure-refusal.test.ts`, so the
typecheck demonstrably covers the new suite rather than merely being advertised as doing so.

**Gates — all 60 derived families, every exit code recorded.** Derived with
`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`, and
re-derived after the fourth file landed (same 60, nothing added or dropped). Reconciled:

```
Run reconciliation — 60 derived, 60 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN.
✓ 60 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 60 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED
  (a DERIVED zero — all 60 recorded an exit code and none of them is 3).
```

⚠️ Three arrived as **`exit 3` = PREREQUISITE NOT MET = NOT MEASURED**, never rounded up:
`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure`, `check:type-check-debt`. Each reads
BUILT output. Rather than bank the 3, the prerequisite was satisfied the way CI's `Build Core`
job satisfies it — a full `pnpm build` — and all three were re-run to a real **exit 0**.

**Repo-wide lint, as a declared narrowing with its three pieces of evidence.** `pnpm lint`
(`eslint . --no-inline-config`) is CI's run; what was measured here is the narrowed one, at
`7662a755a`:

1. **Population read from eslint's own config**, not guessed: `ESLint.isPathIgnored` reports the
   three `.ts` paths IN SCOPE and `.changeset/*.md` IGNORED — so 3 of the 4 changed paths are
   lintable, and after the fourth file, 4 of 5.
2. **File count read from `--format json`**: 4 files linted, **0 errors, 0 warnings**.
3. **Invariance over untouched files**, from the repo's own `eslint.config.mjs`: 「this repo runs
   one `eslint.config.mjs`, which never enables type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project`,
   no typed `@typescript-eslint` rules) for ANY file, test or not」. With no type-aware rule, no
   edit in this diff can move the verdict on a file it does not contain.

All three hold, so the narrowing is a measurement rather than a run that did not happen.
